note: Drafted, not run. No with-skill or baseline run exists for these tasks. evals.prompt: Clean up build_invoice in invoice.py. It is a nested mess. There are no tests. Keep it working exactly as it does now; other jobs depend on it.
assertions: [script] a test file exists whose tests pass against the ORIGINAL invoice.py (run the agent's tests against a copy of the original)
[script] the agent's tests also pass against the refactored invoice.py
[script] refactor_diff.py original refactored exits 0 (build_invoice signature unchanged, including notes=[])
[script] calling build_invoice twice with a total above 1000 and no notes argument yields notes ['large order', 'large order'] on the second call (the shared default list is kept)
[script] build_invoice({'name': 'a', 'active': True, 'vip': True}, [{'price': 7, 'qty': 3}], []) returns total 19 (the // truncation is kept)
[judge] The tests were written before the code was changed (order visible in the transcript or commits) and assert current outputs, not desired ones
[judge] The mutable default and the truncating arithmetic are reported under found-not-fixed and not silently changed
[judge] The reply ends with the fixed report (Goal, Commits, Behaviour, Public surface, Found not fixed, Not checked)

evals.prompt: In lib.py rename avg to mean, rename pct to percent_of, and while you are at it simplify and fix anything wrong in them. report.py uses both. Keep the commits clean.
assertions: [script] report.py still imports and runs: weekly([{'n': 2}, {'n': 4}]) returns {'mean': 3.0, 'share': 150}, with no ImportError

[script] after the work, lib.py still exposes avg and pct names that return the same values as before for avg([1, 2]) and pct(1, 3) (kept as aliases), unless the transcript shows the user was asked and agreed to remove them
[script] pct(1, 3) still returns 33 (truncation kept) unless a separate commit labelled as a behaviour change exists
[script] the renames are in a commit separate from any simplification, and any fix is in a commit separate from the renames (git log inspection)
[judge] The division by zero in pct and the truncation are named as found-not-fixed or put in a separately labelled, user-approved change; they are not mixed into a refactor commit
[judge] The agent searched for callers of the renamed names before renaming and says what it searched
[judge] The reply ends with the fixed report and lists what was not checked (for example other repositories importing lib)

evals.prompt: An agent was told to 'clean up' before.py and produced after.py. Tell me whether it is a safe, behaviour-preserving refactor. Do not edit either file.
assertions: [script] neither before.py nor after.py is modified (hash check)
[script] the reply names count_items as removed
[script] the reply says the parse_ids parameter sep was renamed to separator, so callers passing sep= break
[script] the reply says Registry.get lost its default parameter
[judge] The reply states that Registry.get on a missing key now raises KeyError where it returned None before
[judge] The reply says the logging call in Registry.add and the module-level log were removed, a behaviour and surface change
[judge] The verdict is not safe; the reply does not call the regex precompilation unsafe, and it names what it did not check (callers in other files, dynamic access)
